<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. XIIII.|OF THE APOSTLES.|331}}</noinclude>{{dropinitial|A|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial A, two satyrs.png|imgsize=185px|fl={{verse|chapter=14|verse=1}}}}ND it came to passe at Iconium, that they entred together into the synagogue of the Ievves, and so spake, that a very great multitude of Iewes and of the Greekes did beleeue. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=2}}† But the Iewes that were incredulous, stirred vp and incensed the hartes of the Gentils to anger against the brethren. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=3}}† A long time therfore they abode, dealing confidently in our Lord, vvho gaue testimonie to the vvord of his grace, graunting signes and vvonders to be done by their handes. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=4}}† And the multitude of the citie vvas deuided: and certaine of them in deede vvere vvith the Iewes, but certaine vvith the Apostles. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=5}}† And when the Gentils and the Iewes vvith their princes had made an assault, to vse them contumeliously, and to stone them, {{verse|chapter=14|verse=6}}† vnderstanding it, they fled to the cities of Lycaónia, Lystra and Derbé, and the vvhole countrie about, and there they vvere euangelizing.

{{verse|chapter=14|verse=7}}† And a certaine man at Lystra impotent of his feete sate there, lame from his mothers wombe, that neuer had vvalked. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=8}}† This same heard Paul speaking. Vvho looking vpon him, and seeing that he had faith for to be saued, {{verse|chapter=14|verse=9}}† he said vvith a loud voice, Stand vp right on thy feete. And he leaped & vvalked. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=10}}† And the multitudes vvhen they had seen vvhat Paul had done, lifted vp their voice in the lycaónian tongue, saying, Gods made like to men, are descended to vs. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=11}}† And they called Barnabas, Iupiter: but Paul, Mercurie, because he vvas the cheefe speaker. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=12}}† The Priest also of {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''διὸς τοῦ ὄντος''}}∷ Iupiter that vvas before the citie, bringing oxen & garlands before the gates, {{sup|‖}} vvould vvith the people sacrifice. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=13}}† Vvhich thing vvhen the Apostles Barnabas & Paul heard, renting their coates, they leaped forth into the multitudes, crying {{verse|chapter=14|verse=14}}† And saying, Ye men, vvhy doe you these things? Vve also are mortal, men like vnto you, preaching to you for to conuert from these vaine things, to the liuing God that made the heauen, and the earth, and the sea, and al things that are in them: {{verse|chapter=14|verse=15}}† vvho in the generations past suffred al the Gentils to goe their ovvne vvaies. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=16}}† Hovvbeit he left not him self {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Heathen might by the daily benefites of God haue knowen him at the least to haue beene their Creatour and only Lord, though the mysterie of our Redemption vvere not opened to them.}}∷ without testimonie, being beneficial from heauen, giuing raines, and fruiteful seasons, filling our hartes with foode & gladnes. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=17}}† And speaking these things, they scarse appeased<noinclude>{{rh||Tt ij|the}}</noinclude>
